To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the E2-L210 substitution in CHIKV enhances vector switching to Aedes albopicotus mosquitoes, but not to A. aegpti mosquitoes, and this mutation was selected in the 2009 CHIKV epidemic in Kerala, India.

the ability of chikungunya virus to infect and disseminate in the mosquito vector, Aedes albopicitus, is enhanced by a sequential adaptive mutation, E2-LQ, in addition to the initial adaptive mutation, E1-AV, which was first identified in 2005.
the adaptation of CHIKV and other arboviruses to a new vector species involves the sequential acquisition of mutations that act in a synergistic fashion to enhance virus transmission and spread.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of arthropod-bone (arbo) viruses, particularly chikungunya virus.
the evolution of Chikungunya virus (CHIK), which causes a painful arthritic disease.
the molecular mechanisms of arthropod-boron virus transmission, which is a critical determinant for the emergence of new human viral diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the A226V substitution in the CHIKV E1 protein is the first adaptive mutation in CHIKV that allowed the virus to switch from its primary mosquito vector, Aedes aegypt i, to its secondary vector, Aedes albop ictus, and this was the first mutation that allowed the virus the ability to be transmitted by Aedes albop ic tus, which is the mosquito responsible for spreading the virus from person to person.
the E2- L210Q mutation is a secondary adaptive mutation that increases the fitness of CHIKV in the vector, Aedes albopicitus.

the E1-A226 and E2-L210 mutations in the CHIKV genome are both necessary and sufficient for CHIKV adaptation in Aedes albopicuts, and that the E2-L210 mutation has a significant impact on virus transmission in this vector species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adaptation of Chikugunya virus to a new vector is a complex process that requires the sequential accumulation of multiple adaptive mutations.
we have identified the second adaptive mutation, E2-210 in CHIKV.

the E1-A226 and E2-L210 amino acid substitutions in the CHIKV E1 and E2 envelope glycoproteins, respectively, enhance CHIKV vector switching to A. albipictus, and the sequential acquisition of these mutations is likely to have contributed to the ongoing emergence of CHIKV in a series of epidemics since 2005.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the adaptation of a mosquito-borne virus to its vector involves sequential adaptive mutations.
the adaptation of Chikugunya virus to its new mosquito vector, Aedes albopicitus, involved two sequential mutations in the viral envelope glycoproteins, E1 and E2.
the adaptation of CHIKV in A. albipictus mosquitoes is a continuous process, and that the virus continues to evolve after the initial adaptive E1-A226 V mutation.
